Pantry Shelf Measurements Chart

Two good sources give slightly different numbers, so here they are side by side. Use them as a range rather than a rule.

The two agree on the bottom shelf and differ a little on depth. Go deeper in a walk-in pantry full of bulk food, and shallower in a reach-in pantry, where anything behind the front row is easy to forget. Dimensions.com also puts the comfortable maximum reach at about 69 to 76 inches, so keep everyday food below that and use the very top shelf for backups.

Walk-In Pantry Layouts and Aisle Widths

Before you choose shelves, check that the walkway still works. Dimensions.com lists 36, 42 and 48 inches as typical walk-in pantry aisle widths, and 60 to 66 inches where a wheelchair needs to turn. Add the depth of the shelves on each shelved side, and you get the minimum width of the room.

A U-shape gives the most storage but needs the widest room. A galley, with shelves on two facing walls, suits a long, narrow pantry. If your walk-in is under about 5 feet wide, shelves on one wall, or deep shelves on one side and shallow ones opposite, keep the aisle comfortable.

How to Make Wire Pantry Shelves Work

Many builder-grade pantries come with white wire shelves. You don’t have to rip them out; a few cheap fixes make them far easier to live with:

  • Add a shelf liner. A clear or solid liner cut to size gives jars and bottles a flat surface, so nothing tips through the gaps.
  • Use risers and turntables. A step riser lifts the back row of cans into view, and a turntable stops oils and sauces getting lost in a corner.
  • Group food in matching bins. Same-size bins sit flat across the wires and slide out like drawers.
  • Put heavy jars on solid shelves. If you mix shelf types, keep wire for light boxes and bags, and use wood or laminate for glass jars and tins.

Step by Step: Build Cleat Pantry Shelves

  1. Mark the shelf lines. Use the measurements chart above to set each height, then draw a level line on the back and side walls and mark every stud.
  2. Fix the cleats. Cut 1x2 or 1x3 strips to length and screw them along each line, into at least two studs per strip.
  3. Cut the shelves. Use 3/4 in plywood or pine boards cut to the depth you chose. Where two shelves meet in a corner, overlap them or add a short cleat underneath to carry both.
  4. Stiffen long shelves. Glue and nail a 1x2 strip to the front edge. It hides the plywood layers and helps stop the shelf sagging under jars and cans.
  5. Finish before loading. Fill the screw holes, caulk the joints, then prime and paint with a durable semi-gloss or enamel so spills wipe off. Let the paint cure before you load the shelves.
How to Plan Pantry Shelves in 5 Steps

Lighting and Doors for Pantry Shelves

Light makes deep shelves much easier to use. LED strips fixed under the front edge of each shelf light the shelf below without glare, and battery motion-sensor lights are an easy fix for a closet pantry with no wiring. For hard-wired lights or a new outlet, hire an electrician.

The door matters too. A sliding, pocket or barn door doesn’t swing into the pantry, so it leaves room for shelves on every wall. A hinged door is the one to keep if you want a rack on the back of it, like idea #6.

What is the best shelving for a pantry?

For most homes, adjustable shelving is the best choice, because you can move each shelf to fit what you store. Sealed wood or laminate gives a flat, solid surface for jars, while wire is cheaper and airier but needs a liner for small items. Keep eye-level shelves shallow enough that nothing hides.

How wide should a walk-in pantry be?

Allow at least 36 inches of clear aisle, or 42 to 48 inches for a roomier walk-in, then add the shelf depth on each shelved side. With 16 inch shelves on two facing walls, the room needs to be about 68 inches wide; with shelves on one wall only, about 52 inches.

How high should the top pantry shelf be?

Dimensions.com puts a typical top pantry shelf around 84 inches from the floor, but most people can only reach about 69 to 76 inches without a step. Use the top shelf for backups and rarely used items, keep a step stool nearby and store heavy things low.
